items.heading: The Career Blocker Check
items.text: The Career Blocker Check is a simple way to choose. Find the sentence that sounds most like your week, then build the skill next to it. If two apply, take the earlier one first, because fixing a later problem will not help while an earlier one is still open.

rows: Early career, roughly the first few years
You own tasks now, but someone else sets the priorities.
Data and reporting on your own work, one tool at real depth, clear updates to your manager.
Switching tools every few months and never getting deep in one.
A before-and-after: what you changed, what improved, how you know.
Mid career, roughly five to ten years in
Meetings, people, deadlines. Learning time comes from evenings and weekends.
Stakeholder handling, a multiplier skill (sales sense, analytics, AI-assisted workflow design), people leadership if it suits you.
Treating a management title as the only way up when a specialist or advisory path fits you better.
A process win, a team result or a client outcome you can describe with numbers.
Fragmented time. Short, repeatable study windows.
One refreshed core skill, current tool fluency, and a clear one-line story for the gap.
Trying to rebuild everything at once and burning out in the first stretch.
One small paid or volunteer piece of work done recently, plus an updated profile.

items.heading: Read the Reality
items.text: Read the reality. Open five current job posts for the role you want and note the tools and tasks that repeat.

items.heading: Talk to One Person
items.text: Talk to one person. Ask someone in the role what a normal week looks like, including the boring parts.

items.heading: Do One Small Task
items.text: Do one small task. A tiny version of the real work: a sheet, a short piece of writing, a small build, a process map.

items.heading: Ask for Feedback
items.text: Ask for feedback. Show it to one person in the field. Ask: "Would this get shortlisted where you work?".

visuals.heading: Clear Written English

items.heading: Clear Written English
items.text: Clear written English. A short email that says what you need and by when. If English is your second language, write in short, plain sentences. Being clear matters more than sounding fancy.

items.heading: Spreadsheets
items.text: Spreadsheets. Sorting, filters, simple formulas and a chart. It supports almost every field.

items.heading: Safe AI Use
items.text: Safe AI use. Use AI to draft and research, then check the output yourself, and never paste confidential client or company data into a public tool.

items.heading: Self
items.text: Self-management. Keeping your own task list, meeting a deadline without reminders, telling your manager early when something slips.
